# online-tool

## Websites for Making .ico Files

<blockquote class="link-card">
  
  <h1>Real Favicon Generator</h1>
  
  <a href="https://realfavicongenerator.net/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">realfavicongenerator.net</a>
  
  <small class="link-card-archive">
    (<a href="https://web.archive.org/web/20251128210135/https://realfavicongenerator.net/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">archive</a>)
  </small>
  
</blockquote>




An all-in-one automagic, free and fast site where you upload an image and it generates "icons" for you.
This *includes* a multi-resolution `favicon.ico`, but also icons for various other icon-using platforms, and it gives you little adjustable previews of each of those so you can get something that'll look right everywhere.

For a favicon it's super-simple - upload, next, download, done.

<blockquote class="link-card">
  
  <h1>RedKetchup Icon Editor</h1>
  
  <a href="https://redketchup.io/icon-editor/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">redketchup.io/icon-editor</a>
  
  <small class="link-card-archive">
    (<a href="https://web.archive.org/web/20251129031359/https://redketchup.io/icon-editor" target="_blank" rel="noopener">archive</a>)
  </small>
  
</blockquote>




If you need a little more hands-on control of your icon creation, this editor gives you a pixel editing GUI for each resolution that will be included in your icon.
This lets you fix display errors from automatic scaling, and choose to exclude or include additional resolutions.

It works for favicons, but it *shines* for PC icons, where it's almost certain that the beautiful 512x512 version of your graphic isn't going to look correct when *automatically* downscaled to 16x16.
